title: What If a Zombie Fungus Could Infect Humans? Experts Weigh In

scenes.text: What if the zombie fungus that controls ants could jump to humans? Scientists say it can't.
Ophiocordyceps makes an infected ant climb a leaf, clamp down, and wait while spores grow from its head.
It works like a key for one lock. Each species is tuned to a single kind of insect.
No Ophiocordyceps species is known to infect fish, amphibians or mammals.
Warm bodies are the real wall. Most fungi can't survive human body heat of about 37 degrees Celsius.
The CDC's Tom Chiller says it took millions of years to adapt to ants. Humans would need the same.
